title: Public host, database, vhost and user parts of connection strings
summary: Connection strings and key-value strings that carry only public parts: host, port, database, replica or cluster name, AMQP vhost (including %2F), user name, and Windows integrated authentication, with no password slot.
rationale: Host and database names are the metadata a reader needs and a reviewer should see; the user name is an identifier, not a secret. Reporting them makes logs and configs unreadable without hiding anything. Keeping these public parts recorded separately from the password span is what lets the positive cases demand an exact password range rather than the whole string.

expectation.rationale: The cited grammars define user-info, host, port, path or database and options as separate components, and the password as a distinct optional part; strings with no password component contain no password. Integrated Security=SSPI is documented as the Windows authentication form that takes no user name or password.

sources.supports: mongodb+srv:// strings may carry only a host and options; the credentials, when present, are the user-info before the host.
sources.locator: section "Find Your Self-Hosted Deployment's Connection String" and the cluster example

sources.supports: amqp_userinfo is optional; the vhost is a separate path component and percent-encoded octets in it are decoded before it is passed to the server (%2F is a vhost named /).
sources.locator: sections "Virtual Host" and "The amqp URI scheme"

sources.supports: Windows authentication is selected with Integrated Security=SSPI (or true) and needs no user name or password in the string.
A connection URI is postgresql://[userspec@][hostspec][/dbname][?paramspec]; keyword/value pairs such as host, port, dbname are separate settings.
